---
### Review: typing `Decoder.Config.layers` as `list[TransformerBlock.Config]`

- [x] Gather context (diff, affected files)
- [x] Review typing changes and casts
- [x] Check all callsites / model variants
- [x] Post review

Tightening the `decoder.py` annotation makes sense. A few things need fixing before this can merge, though. The first one is a blocker.

---

### 1. Blocker: `Resolves #2936` will close the TODO debt tracker issue

#2936 isn't a normal issue. `.github/workflows/todo_debt_tracker.yaml` (line 58, `ISSUE_NUMBER: 2936`) rewrites its body every day, and the job errors out when the issue isn't open:

```yaml
if [ "$STATE" != "OPEN" ]; then
  echo "Error: Issue #$ISSUE_NUMBER is currently $STATE. "
  exit 1
```

Merging this PR as written closes #2936, and after that the tracker fails on every push to main and on every daily cron run. Please change the PR body to `Part of #2936` or `Addresses a TODO tracked in #2936`.

### 2. Lint: new imports are out of order and duplicate an existing import path

`TransformerBlock` is already re-exported from `torchtitan.models.common` (`common/__init__.py:38`). llama3, qwen3, gpt_oss, deepseek_v3 and kimi_k2_7 all import it from that existing `from torchtitan.models.common import (...)` block. The new imports are separate `from torchtitan.models.common.decoder import TransformerBlock` lines, and three of them sit in a spot usort/ufmt will reject:
- `kimi_k3/flavors.py:24` comes before `from torchtitan.models.common import (`
- `muse_glimmer/flavors.py:26` comes before `from torchtitan.models.common.attention import`
- `qwen3_5/flavors.py:35` comes before `from torchtitan.models.common.attention.gdn import`

Please add `TransformerBlock` to each file's existing `torchtitan.models.common` import list, including `deepseek_v4/flavors.py:43`, and run `pre-commit run --all-files`.

### 3. The `list` casts can be avoided by following the existing pattern

The other models already handle invariance without a cast. Their builders return `list[TransformerBlock.Config]` and append into a list typed as the base class (`llama3/flavors.py:85-89`, `qwen3/flavors.py:116`, `gpt_oss/flavors.py:222`, `deepseek_v3/flavors.py:299`). In qwen3_5, muse_glimmer, deepseek_v4 and kimi_k3 you could do the same:

```python
layers: list[TransformerBlock.Config] = []
...
return layers
```

Adding a `Qwen35TransformerBlock.Config` to a `list[TransformerBlock.Config]` type-checks fine, so the `cast(list[TransformerBlock.Config], layers)` calls and their `from typing import cast` imports can go. That keeps every model on one idiom.

The one exception is DeepSeek V4. `_build_mtp_layers` needs the subclass-typed `layers[-1]` (`deepseek_v4/flavors.py:856/1002/1148`), so the element-level `cast(DeepSeekV4TransformerBlock.Config, layers[-1])` is fine to keep.

### 4. The `getattr(..., default)` calls in state dict adapters can hide errors

This goes against CLAUDE.md principle 7 (no speculative fallbacks).

- **`deepseek_v3/state_dict_adapter.py:71`**: `getattr(model_config.layers[0].attention, "q_lora_rank", 0)`. The PR description says the `0` matches the `Attention.Config` default, but `q_lora_rank` isn't defined on `Attention.Config`. It's only on `DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config` (`deepseek_v3/model.py:53`). If the attention config is ever not MLA, or the field gets renamed, this quietly picks the non-LoRA HF key map, and the only symptom is wrong or missing keys at checkpoint load. That's the kind of loading breakage `.claude/rules/models.md` asks us to protect against.
- **`kimi_k3/state_dict_adapter.py:269`**: `getattr(self.kimi_config.layers[0], "attention_res_norm", None)`. `attention_res_norm` is a required field with no default on `KimiK3TransformerBlock.Config` (`kimi_k3/model.py:240`). The `None` fallback would make the adapter generate placeholder layer-0 attn-res weights for any config that lacks the attribute.

Narrowing the type explicitly would satisfy the type checker and still fail loudly, for example:

```python
attention = model_config.layers[0].attention
assert isinstance(attention, DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config)
if attention.q_lora_rank != 0:
```

and

```python
layer0 = self.kimi_config.layers[0]
assert isinstance(layer0, KimiK3TransformerBlock.Config)
if layer0.attention_res_norm is None:
```

`cast(...)` would also work, though it skips the runtime check.

### 5. A TODO for a different discussion was removed (`deepseek_v3/model.py:88`)

The deleted `TODO(fegin)` linked to `discussion_r3034078575`. That's a different review thread from the `layers` typing one (`r3033849265`), and nothing in this diff changes how `wkv_a`/`kv_norm`/`wkv_b` are built. The replacement comment ("MLA projection shapes live on each Linear.Config…") doesn't show the original concern was resolved. Unless @fegin confirms that thread is done, please restore the TODO, or move this change to its own PR. Otherwise the debt tracker loses an item that's still open.

### 6. Smaller notes

- **`kimi_k3/model.py`**: dropping the `layers: list[KimiK3TransformerBlock.Config]` override is fine at runtime, since the field is `kw_only` and still required on the base. But code in `kimi_k3/` that reads subclass-only fields from `config.layers[i]` now gets weaker static types. Item 4 covers the adapter; a quick check of the other kimi_k3 callsites would be worth doing.
- **`deepseek_v3/mtp.py:202`**: typing `mtp_layers: list[MTPTransformerBlock.Config]` matches `_build_mtp_layers` (`deepseek_v3/flavors.py:424`). DeepSeek V4 builds its own `list[MTPBlock.Config]` and doesn't go through `MTPDecoder.Config`, so this doesn't affect it.
- **Verification**: the unit tests listed don't exercise either state dict adapter. Since the adapters changed, please run a quick HF key mapping check for DeepSeek V3/Kimi K2.7, which goes through the same `q_lora_rank` branch, and for Kimi K3. A CPU `from_hf` key-set check would be enough.

### Summary

| Item | Severity |
|---|---|
| `Resolves #2936` would close the TODO tracker issue and break its workflow | **Blocker** |
| New imports are out of order and duplicate the `torchtitan.models.common` export | Lint failure |
| `getattr` fallbacks in DeepSeek V3 / Kimi K3 state dict adapters | Should fix |
| Unrelated TODO removed in `deepseek_v3/model.py` | Should fix |
| `cast(list[...])` instead of the existing base-typed list pattern | Nit / consistency |

I didn't run `pre-commit` or `pyrefly` in this job. The lint finding comes from reading the import order, so please confirm it locally.

---
### Re-review: typing `Decoder.Config.layers` as `list[TransformerBlock.Config]`

- [x] Gather the diff, including the new commit `27628a1`
- [x] Check which items from the previous review were addressed
- [x] Look for new issues
- [x] Post review

Commit `27628a1` addresses most of the previous review. It also adds a regression that breaks the DeepSeek V4 state dict adapter, and that has to be fixed before merge.

---

### What's fixed since the last review

| Previous item | Status |
|---|---|
| `Resolves #2936` would close the TODO tracker | ✅ The body now says `Part of #2936` |
| Imports out of order and duplicating the `torchtitan.models.common` export | ✅ `TransformerBlock` is now in each file's existing `torchtitan.models.common` import list |
| `cast(list[...])` instead of the base-typed list pattern | ✅ Builders now return `list[TransformerBlock.Config]` with `layers: list[TransformerBlock.Config] = []`. The element-level `cast(DeepSeekV4TransformerBlock.Config, layers[-1])` stays, which is fine. |
| `getattr` fallbacks in the state dict adapters | ⚠️ Replaced with `assert isinstance`, but the DeepSeek V3 one breaks V4 (see below) |
| Unrelated `TODO(fegin)` removed from `deepseek_v3/model.py` | ✅ Restored. `deepseek_v3/model.py` no longer appears in the net diff. |

### 1. Blocker: the new assert in `DeepSeekV3StateDictAdapter.__init__` fails for every DeepSeek V4 config

`torchtitan/models/deepseek_v3/state_dict_adapter.py:72-76`:

```python
from .model import DeepSeekMLAAttention

attention = model_config.layers[0].attention
assert isinstance(attention, DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config)
```

`DeepSeekV4StateDictAdapter` subclasses this adapter and calls `super().__init__(model_config, hf_assets_path)` (`deepseek_v4/state_dict_adapter.py:31`). V4 layers use `DeepSeekV4Attention.Config`, and that class inherits from `Attention.Config`, not from `DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config` (`deepseek_v4/attention.py:273`). So the assert raises `AssertionError` whenever a V4 adapter is constructed. That breaks:
- every V4 HF checkpoint load and save (`from_hf` / `to_hf`)
- `DeepSeekV4StateDictAdapterTest` in `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/test_state_dict_adapter.py:301` and `:357`, which build `DeepSeekV4StateDictAdapter(config, ...)` directly

Before this PR the code worked by duck typing: both config classes define `q_lora_rank`. V4 then overwrites `self.from_hf_map` completely (`deepseek_v4/state_dict_adapter.py:33`), so the V3 `q_lora_rank` branch never had any effect for V4.

Two ways to fix it:
- **Recommended:** move the V3 map construction, including the `q_lora_rank` branch, into a method such as `_build_from_hf_map(model_config)`. V4 overrides that method rather than calling the V3 map logic and then throwing the result away. The V3 assert is then only reached with V3/Kimi K2.7 configs, which use `DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config` (`deepseek_v3/flavors.py:218`). This also removes the existing `# pyrefly: ignore [bad-argument-type]` workaround's reason for existing.
- **Minimal:** keep the narrowing but don't depend on the concrete class. For example, use `cast(DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config, ...)` with a comment that V4's config also has `q_lora_rank` and V4 replaces the map anyway. Checking against `DeepSeekV4Attention.Config` from V3 code would add a reverse V3 → V4 dependency, so avoid that.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20cursor%2Fdecoder-layers-typing-ab29%2C%20torchtitan%2Fmodels%2Fdeepseek_v3%2Fstate_dict_adapter.py%20lines%2070-89%20assert%20isinstance(attention%2C%20DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config)%20which%20fails%20for%20DeepSeekV4StateDictAdapter%20(it%20calls%20super().__init__%20and%20V4%20uses%20DeepSeekV4Attention.Config).%20Move%20from_hf_map%20construction%20into%20an%20overridable%20method%20that%20DeepSeekV4StateDictAdapter%20overrides%2C%20then%20run%20pytest%20tests%2Funit_tests%2Fcpu%2Fmodels%2Ftest_state_dict_adapter.py&repo=pytorch/torchtitan)

### 2. Kimi K3 adapter assert looks fine

`kimi_k3/state_dict_adapter.py:270-274` narrows to `KimiK3TransformerBlock.Config`. Kimi K3 is the only user of this adapter, and its layer builder only creates `KimiK3TransformerBlock.Config` (`kimi_k3/flavors.py:604`), so the assert holds.

### 3. Nits

- **Function-level imports.** The comment "model.py imports this adapter before the class exists" is accurate: `deepseek_v3/model.py:34` and `kimi_k3/model.py:66` import the adapter at module level. For the type-narrowing part alone, `if TYPE_CHECKING:` plus `cast` would avoid the import at runtime, but you need the real class for `isinstance`, so the local import is reasonable if you keep the asserts.
- **Tests.** The PR description lists `test_configurable.py` and `test_tp_kv_heads_validation.py`. Please also run `pytest tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/test_state_dict_adapter.py`, which covers the V3 and V4 adapters and would have caught item 1. The Kimi K3 adapter test is GPU-only (`tests/unit_tests/gpu/models/kimi_k3/test_kimi_k3.py:310`).

### Summary

| Item | Severity |
|---|---|
| `isinstance(..., DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config)` assert breaks `DeepSeekV4StateDictAdapter` | **Blocker** |
| Run `test_state_dict_adapter.py` (CPU) before re-requesting review | Should do |
| Everything else from the previous review | Addressed |

I worked this out from the code. I couldn't run `pytest`, `pre-commit` or `pyrefly` in this job because shell commands need approval that this job doesn't have. The V4 failure follows directly from the class hierarchy (`DeepSeekV4Attention.Config(Attention.Config)`) and the `super().__init__` call.

If we remove no pyre errors but introduces more (linter CI shows more errors), the solution is not correct. 

Please see if the Generic solution can help.

Probably try:

```
  class Config(BaseModel.Config, Generic[LayerConfigT]):
      layers: list[LayerConfigT]
```

---
### Review: typing `Decoder.Config.layers` as `list[TransformerBlock.Config]`

- [x] Gather context (diff, affected files)
- [x] Review typing changes and casts
- [x] Check all callsites / model variants
- [x] Post review

Tightening the `decoder.py` annotation makes sense. A few things need fixing before this can merge, though. The first one is a blocker.

---

### 1. Blocker: `Resolves #2936` will close the TODO debt tracker issue

#2936 isn't a normal issue. `.github/workflows/todo_debt_tracker.yaml` (line 58, `ISSUE_NUMBER: 2936`) rewrites its body every day, and the job errors out when the issue isn't open:

```yaml
if [ "$STATE" != "OPEN" ]; then
  echo "Error: Issue #$ISSUE_NUMBER is currently $STATE. "
  exit 1
```

Merging this PR as written closes #2936, and after that the tracker fails on every push to main and on every daily cron run. Please change the PR body to `Part of #2936` or `Addresses a TODO tracked in #2936`.

### 2. Lint: new imports are out of order and duplicate an existing import path

`TransformerBlock` is already re-exported from `torchtitan.models.common` (`common/__init__.py:38`). llama3, qwen3, gpt_oss, deepseek_v3 and kimi_k2_7 all import it from that existing `from torchtitan.models.common import (...)` block. The new imports are separate `from torchtitan.models.common.decoder import TransformerBlock` lines, and three of them sit in a spot usort/ufmt will reject:
- `kimi_k3/flavors.py:24` comes before `from torchtitan.models.common import (`
- `muse_glimmer/flavors.py:26` comes before `from torchtitan.models.common.attention import`
- `qwen3_5/flavors.py:35` comes before `from torchtitan.models.common.attention.gdn import`

Please add `TransformerBlock` to each file's existing `torchtitan.models.common` import list, including `deepseek_v4/flavors.py:43`, and run `pre-commit run --all-files`.

### 3. The `list` casts can be avoided by following the existing pattern

The other models already handle invariance without a cast. Their builders return `list[TransformerBlock.Config]` and append into a list typed as the base class (`llama3/flavors.py:85-89`, `qwen3/flavors.py:116`, `gpt_oss/flavors.py:222`, `deepseek_v3/flavors.py:299`). In qwen3_5, muse_glimmer, deepseek_v4 and kimi_k3 you could do the same:

```python
layers: list[TransformerBlock.Config] = []
...
return layers
```

Adding a `Qwen35TransformerBlock.Config` to a `list[TransformerBlock.Config]` type-checks fine, so the `cast(list[TransformerBlock.Config], layers)` calls and their `from typing import cast` imports can go. That keeps every model on one idiom.

The one exception is DeepSeek V4. `_build_mtp_layers` needs the subclass-typed `layers[-1]` (`deepseek_v4/flavors.py:856/1002/1148`), so the element-level `cast(DeepSeekV4TransformerBlock.Config, layers[-1])` is fine to keep.

### 4. The `getattr(..., default)` calls in state dict adapters can hide errors

This goes against CLAUDE.md principle 7 (no speculative fallbacks).

- **`deepseek_v3/state_dict_adapter.py:71`**: `getattr(model_config.layers[0].attention, "q_lora_rank", 0)`. The PR description says the `0` matches the `Attention.Config` default, but `q_lora_rank` isn't defined on `Attention.Config`. It's only on `DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config` (`deepseek_v3/model.py:53`). If the attention config is ever not MLA, or the field gets renamed, this quietly picks the non-LoRA HF key map, and the only symptom is wrong or missing keys at checkpoint load. That's the kind of loading breakage `.claude/rules/models.md` asks us to protect against.
- **`kimi_k3/state_dict_adapter.py:269`**: `getattr(self.kimi_config.layers[0], "attention_res_norm", None)`. `attention_res_norm` is a required field with no default on `KimiK3TransformerBlock.Config` (`kimi_k3/model.py:240`). The `None` fallback would make the adapter generate placeholder layer-0 attn-res weights for any config that lacks the attribute.

Narrowing the type explicitly would satisfy the type checker and still fail loudly, for example:

```python
attention = model_config.layers[0].attention
assert isinstance(attention, DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config)
if attention.q_lora_rank != 0:
```

and

```python
layer0 = self.kimi_config.layers[0]
assert isinstance(layer0, KimiK3TransformerBlock.Config)
if layer0.attention_res_norm is None:
```

`cast(...)` would also work, though it skips the runtime check.

### 5. A TODO for a different discussion was removed (`deepseek_v3/model.py:88`)

The deleted `TODO(fegin)` linked to `discussion_r3034078575`. That's a different review thread from the `layers` typing one (`r3033849265`), and nothing in this diff changes how `wkv_a`/`kv_norm`/`wkv_b` are built. The replacement comment ("MLA projection shapes live on each Linear.Config…") doesn't show the original concern was resolved. Unless @fegin confirms that thread is done, please restore the TODO, or move this change to its own PR. Otherwise the debt tracker loses an item that's still open.

### 6. Smaller notes

- **`kimi_k3/model.py`**: dropping the `layers: list[KimiK3TransformerBlock.Config]` override is fine at runtime, since the field is `kw_only` and still required on the base. But code in `kimi_k3/` that reads subclass-only fields from `config.layers[i]` now gets weaker static types. Item 4 covers the adapter; a quick check of the other kimi_k3 callsites would be worth doing.
- **`deepseek_v3/mtp.py:202`**: typing `mtp_layers: list[MTPTransformerBlock.Config]` matches `_build_mtp_layers` (`deepseek_v3/flavors.py:424`). DeepSeek V4 builds its own `list[MTPBlock.Config]` and doesn't go through `MTPDecoder.Config`, so this doesn't affect it.
- **Verification**: the unit tests listed don't exercise either state dict adapter. Since the adapters changed, please run a quick HF key mapping check for DeepSeek V3/Kimi K2.7, which goes through the same `q_lora_rank` branch, and for Kimi K3. A CPU `from_hf` key-set check would be enough.

### Summary

| Item | Severity |
|---|---|
| `Resolves #2936` would close the TODO tracker issue and break its workflow | **Blocker** |
| New imports are out of order and duplicate the `torchtitan.models.common` export | Lint failure |
| `getattr` fallbacks in DeepSeek V3 / Kimi K3 state dict adapters | Should fix |
| Unrelated TODO removed in `deepseek_v3/model.py` | Should fix |
| `cast(list[...])` instead of the existing base-typed list pattern | Nit / consistency |

I didn't run `pre-commit` or `pyrefly` in this job. The lint finding comes from reading the import order, so please confirm it locally.

### Re-review: typing `Decoder.Config.layers` as `list[TransformerBlock.Config]`

- [x] Gather the diff, including the new commit `27628a1`
- [x] Check which items from the previous review were addressed
- [x] Look for new issues
- [x] Post review

Commit `27628a1` addresses most of the previous review. It also adds a regression that breaks the DeepSeek V4 state dict adapter, and that has to be fixed before merge.

---

### What's fixed since the last review

| Previous item | Status |
|---|---|
| `Resolves #2936` would close the TODO tracker | ✅ The body now says `Part of #2936` |
| Imports out of order and duplicating the `torchtitan.models.common` export | ✅ `TransformerBlock` is now in each file's existing `torchtitan.models.common` import list |
| `cast(list[...])` instead of the base-typed list pattern | ✅ Builders now return `list[TransformerBlock.Config]` with `layers: list[TransformerBlock.Config] = []`. The element-level `cast(DeepSeekV4TransformerBlock.Config, layers[-1])` stays, which is fine. |
| `getattr` fallbacks in the state dict adapters | ⚠️ Replaced with `assert isinstance`, but the DeepSeek V3 one breaks V4 (see below) |
| Unrelated `TODO(fegin)` removed from `deepseek_v3/model.py` | ✅ Restored. `deepseek_v3/model.py` no longer appears in the net diff. |

### 1. Blocker: the new assert in `DeepSeekV3StateDictAdapter.__init__` fails for every DeepSeek V4 config

`torchtitan/models/deepseek_v3/state_dict_adapter.py:72-76`:

```python
from .model import DeepSeekMLAAttention

attention = model_config.layers[0].attention
assert isinstance(attention, DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config)
```

`DeepSeekV4StateDictAdapter` subclasses this adapter and calls `super().__init__(model_config, hf_assets_path)` (`deepseek_v4/state_dict_adapter.py:31`). V4 layers use `DeepSeekV4Attention.Config`, and that class inherits from `Attention.Config`, not from `DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config` (`deepseek_v4/attention.py:273`). So the assert raises `AssertionError` whenever a V4 adapter is constructed. That breaks:
- every V4 HF checkpoint load and save (`from_hf` / `to_hf`)
- `DeepSeekV4StateDictAdapterTest` in `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/test_state_dict_adapter.py:301` and `:357`, which build `DeepSeekV4StateDictAdapter(config, ...)` directly

Before this PR the code worked by duck typing: both config classes define `q_lora_rank`. V4 then overwrites `self.from_hf_map` completely (`deepseek_v4/state_dict_adapter.py:33`), so the V3 `q_lora_rank` branch never had any effect for V4.

Two ways to fix it:
- **Recommended:** move the V3 map construction, including the `q_lora_rank` branch, into a method such as `_build_from_hf_map(model_config)`. V4 overrides that method rather than calling the V3 map logic and then throwing the result away. The V3 assert is then only reached with V3/Kimi K2.7 configs, which use `DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config` (`deepseek_v3/flavors.py:218`). This also removes the existing `# pyrefly: ignore [bad-argument-type]` workaround's reason for existing.
- **Minimal:** keep the narrowing but don't depend on the concrete class. For example, use `cast(DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config, ...)` with a comment that V4's config also has `q_lora_rank` and V4 replaces the map anyway. Checking against `DeepSeekV4Attention.Config` from V3 code would add a reverse V3 → V4 dependency, so avoid that.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20cursor%2Fdecoder-layers-typing-ab29%2C%20torchtitan%2Fmodels%2Fdeepseek_v3%2Fstate_dict_adapter.py%20lines%2070-89%20assert%20isinstance(attention%2C%20DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config)%20which%20fails%20for%20DeepSeekV4StateDictAdapter%20(it%20calls%20super().__init__%20and%20V4%20uses%20DeepSeekV4Attention.Config).%20Move%20from_hf_map%20construction%20into%20an%20overridable%20method%20that%20DeepSeekV4StateDictAdapter%20overrides%2C%20then%20run%20pytest%20tests%2Funit_tests%2Fcpu%2Fmodels%2Ftest_state_dict_adapter.py&repo=pytorch/torchtitan)

### 2. Kimi K3 adapter assert looks fine

`kimi_k3/state_dict_adapter.py:270-274` narrows to `KimiK3TransformerBlock.Config`. Kimi K3 is the only user of this adapter, and its layer builder only creates `KimiK3TransformerBlock.Config` (`kimi_k3/flavors.py:604`), so the assert holds.

### 3. Nits

- **Function-level imports.** The comment "model.py imports this adapter before the class exists" is accurate: `deepseek_v3/model.py:34` and `kimi_k3/model.py:66` import the adapter at module level. For the type-narrowing part alone, `if TYPE_CHECKING:` plus `cast` would avoid the import at runtime, but you need the real class for `isinstance`, so the local import is reasonable if you keep the asserts.
- **Tests.** The PR description lists `test_configurable.py` and `test_tp_kv_heads_validation.py`. Please also run `pytest tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/test_state_dict_adapter.py`, which covers the V3 and V4 adapters and would have caught item 1. The Kimi K3 adapter test is GPU-only (`tests/unit_tests/gpu/models/kimi_k3/test_kimi_k3.py:310`).

### Summary

| Item | Severity |
|---|---|
| `isinstance(..., DeepSeekMLAAttention.Config)` assert breaks `DeepSeekV4StateDictAdapter` | **Blocker** |
| Run `test_state_dict_adapter.py` (CPU) before re-requesting review | Should do |
| Everything else from the previous review | Addressed |

I worked this out from the code. I couldn't run `pytest`, `pre-commit` or `pyrefly` in this job because shell commands need approval that this job doesn't have. The V4 failure follows directly from the class hierarchy (`DeepSeekV4Attention.Config(Attention.Config)`) and the `super().__init__` call.
